item.title: Saturday Morning, Oct 31
item.description:
The Saturday morning bulletin from Gumshoe News Radio for October 31, 2026, Halloween: Londonderry weather with the seven-day outlook; the final weekend before the midterms, the Justice Department's widening Alaska push, and court rulings on the NFL's Sunday Ticket and Idaho's abortion law; Poland's president confronts judges inside the top court, France braces for Halloween protests, a two-billion-dollar Patriot sale for Ukraine, Congo's Ebola deaths pass five thousand, and Gulf states urge calm; a weekend look at markets after a rough October; France's proposed tax on every gigabyte; OpenAI trims its funding round and Claude Code stops cloning games; an exploited Ivanti chain, a fixed ChatGPT link flaw and Cloudflare's DDoS numbers; your X feed; Dartmouth's provost resigns over undisclosed A.I. use, plus trick-or-treat and the time change; and a dream wedding at Top of the Rock. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Friday 4 PM Update, Oct 30
item.description:
The Friday four o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 30, 2026: Londonderry conditions through tomorrow afternoon; the Cook Political Report shifts a dozen House races toward Democrats, an appeals court again turns down the Justice Department on California ballots, the president welcomes freed American Stephen Hubbard, and a nationwide "ghost student" aid-fraud case; a standoff over Poland's top court, mixed signals on Iran, and Mayon Volcano erupts; markets near the close as the A.I. selloff caps a rough October; Meta settles another social media addiction case; Google's first A.I. answer from orbit and new ChatGPT limits for teens; an actively exploited GitLab flaw and hundreds of search-hijacking Chrome extensions; your X feed; a record-turnout forecast for New Hampshire; and superhero window washers in Pittsburgh. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Friday 1 PM Update, Oct 30
item.description:
The Friday one o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 30, 2026: Londonderry conditions through tomorrow afternoon; Trump puts the Iowa and Kansas rallies back on, Pope Leo becomes the first pope to vote in a U.S. election, and a Houston ICE officer is charged in a ramming case; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims three tankers burned in Hormuz, Oleshky's evacuation wraps up, and Salvadoran troops pour into Haiti; midday markets as the tech rout deepens and gold hits a one-year low; Foxconn teases a new OpenAI tie-up; Nvidia may back an Anthropic data center's debt and OpenAI joins a shared opt-out signal for A.I. training; a hardware wallet with a suspected spy chip and the Polymarket breach; your X feed; trick-or-treat times around southern New Hampshire; and a Texas school named for its longtime custodian. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Friday 10 AM Update, Oct 30
item.description:
The Friday ten o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 30, 2026: Londonderry conditions through tomorrow morning; the Pentagon refers a fired three-star general for possible prosecution over leaks, early voting runs far ahead of 2022, and a Massachusetts officer's murder trial; Russia's Novaya Gazeta says it's being forced to close, limpet mines on a Hormuz tanker, and Canada and the E.U. launch a new alliance; markets at the open as Intel and Amazon lead a tech rout while Exxon and Chevron beat; SpaceX's filing points to Anthropic as its biggest customer; Wikipedia's operator weighs in on the Times-OpenAI copyright fight; a backdoored Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace; your X feed; live music and the end of daylight saving time here in New Hampshire; and a strawberry farmer who became a mentor by accident. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.
